A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable and describe the same OpenFly platform, 100K-trajectory benchmark, and OpenFly-Agent. Inspection covers all supplied pages, figures, tables, and v5 Appendices A–K; relocated material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original navigation experiments, component ablations, dataset analyses, and manual instruction-quality assessment, including Tables III–V.

after.justification: v5 retains original simulation experiments and adds linguistic analyses and physical-flight evaluations, including Tables 5–7.

M1.justification: The OpenVLA-based agent, keyframe selection, token merging, FIFO memory, and A* trajectory pipeline match. v5 Section 3.2 additionally describes GPT-4o semantic labeling of contour-extracted instances. The PDFs do not establish whether this introduces a procedure or documents a previously omitted implementation step.

E1.justification: v5 Appendix K extends evaluation from simulated navigation to physical flights in 23 outdoor scenes with human-created tasks. It also uses AerialVLN as an alternative training corpus. The original OpenFly benchmark's 100K trajectories and 18 scenes remain.

E2.justification: v5 Table 1 adds NaVILA to both simulation comparisons alongside the retained Random, Seq2Seq, CMA, AerialVLN, and Navid methods. Appendix K also compares against Navid and NaVILA in physical flights. This is a limited expansion of comparator membership.

E3.justification: Reported seen/unseen split sizes change from 1600/1400 to 1800/1200, now matching the 60/40 chart already present in v1; this does not establish that experiments were rerun. v5 adds a physical-flight protocol covering 23 human-created tasks of 50–500 m with external-PC inference and SR/OSR evaluation, plus a linguistic analysis sampling 25 instructions.

E4.justification: v5 adds linguistic-phenomenon analysis, 3D GS navigation cases, and a training-corpus comparison examining real-world transfer. Conversely, v1's easy/moderate/hard performance breakdowns and before/after action-distribution analysis are removed. The keyframe-selection and token-merging ablation is retained, so the change concerns the broader analytical coverage.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or formal significance tests. v5's linguistic proportions and mean frequencies add descriptive results without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: v5 adds NaVILA results and physical-flight results: Table 6 reports 26.09% SR for OpenFly-Agent versus 13.0% for both comparators; Table 7 reports 4.3% SR with AerialVLN training. Difficulty-specific entries disappear. Seq2Seq's reported seen SR changes from 4.0% to 0.1%, and unseen OSR from 3.2% to 0.9%, while OpenFly-Agent's aggregate SR remains 18.5%/5.1%. Revised split counts prevent interpreting these as established same-setting performance changes.

T1.justification: Neither version supplies theoretical guarantees, theorems, or proofs. v5 omits v1's elementary pose and token-set notation, but does not substantively alter the mathematical task, assumptions, or reasoning.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central contributions: automated multi-engine data generation, the largest claimed aerial VLN benchmark with 100K trajectories across 18 scenes, and a superior keyframe-aware agent. Greater emphasis on engine integration and customization does not materially redefine these claims.

C2.justification: v5 interprets the training-corpus comparison as evidence of bridging the sim-to-real gap and further discusses ambiguous landmark descriptions and practical instruction complexity. v1's explanation of poor short-route stopping behavior disappears with the difficulty breakdowns. Reconstruction-artifact and real-time deployment limitations remain.

D1.justification: Appendices B, F, and K newly disclose shooting-altitude and camera-tilt guidance, sample instruction-generation prompts, and flight hardware/offboard inference details. Semantic captioning is also newly documented. Some earlier preprocessing and action-bin details disappear; shared model/token settings and the promise of a future code release remain.

R1.justification: v5 removes the simulator-related-work survey and associated citations such as MuJoCo and Habitat, and drops MatrixCity. It adds NaVILA and discusses OpenUAV's ground-truth-aligned human assistance. The principal positioning against existing aerial VLN benchmarks remains stable.

P1.justification: The title changes, platform descriptions are extensively condensed, dataset splitting moves into dataset analysis, and substantial implementation, quality-control, and qualitative material is reorganized into appendices. Related-work and agent subsections are also streamlined, producing a substantial structural revision beyond the added experiments.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout. Separate difficulty-stratified results tables become one aggregate table; the architecture diagram and scene montage are redesigned, and retained qualitative figures are rearranged or relocated. New word clouds, linguistic and real-flight tables, component visualizations, and navigation figures substantially alter the presentation.

improvement.justification: v5 adds physical-flight validation absent from v1, a competitive NaVILA baseline, and useful collection and prompt details, strengthening practical evidence and reproducibility. The gain is limited: Appendix K covers only 23 tasks with offboard inference and no uncertainty estimates, its whole-corpus comparison does not isolate the contribution of 3D GS data, and removing difficulty-specific results reduces diagnostic depth.
